Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Locations 2 Actions 2.1 Purchase a Wax Seal. 2.2 Research a Specimen if its tile is in the Museum. 3 Personal Board Bonuses for Completed Objectives 4 End Game Scoring Locations The board contains two Main Diaries, a Special Diary, and a Small Diary. A Diary may be divided into Sections by a red bookmark. On their turn, the active player places a worker onto a location to take that location's action. If the location is in a Diary Section with no other workers, there is no cost to placing it. However, if a Diary Section already has workers of any colour (including the active player's), the active player must pay a Coin Penalty. The Coin Penalty is 3 for a 2-player game, 2 otherwise. Circular Magnifying Glass Any number of workers may be placed. Lens Only one worker can be placed. Whenever a player places a worker onto an opponent's Lens, that opponent gains 1 Coin from the supply. Rectangular Magnifying Glass Any number of workers may be placed. There is no Coin Penalty for rectangular magnifying glass locations. Actions After the active player places a worker on a location, they may perform the location's action. Actions may be performed in any order. The player is not required to complete all actions. Unlock Lens Location | Gray Lens Place an unlocked Lens token on a locked Lens location. The active player may immediately perform all actions at this location, ignoring all Wax Seal requirements. This Lens location is now unlocked, and any player may use the location on their turn. The owner of the unlocked Lens will receive 1 Coin from the supply when an opponent places a worker on it. Academy | Red Scroll Purchase a Wax Seal. A Wax Seal costs Coins according to its row. The active player adds the new Wax Seal to the left-most empty spot for any worker, paying the cost of the spot. The 4th and 6th Wax Seal for a worker grants silver and gold distinctions, respectively. Navigation | Blue Tall Ship Move Ship along the Ocean track. Any number of Ships can be on the same Ocean track space. When a Ship crosses a silver banner on the Ocean track, the active player must place an Explorer on the starting space of the corresponding Island. If there is an action icon where the Ship stops, the active player may perform the action. Exploration | Green Boot Move an Explorer along an Island track. Skip spaces occupied by opponent's Explorers. Only one Explorer can be on each Island track space, except for the first and last spaces. When the first Explorer crosses a golden ribbon on an Island track, that player gains victory points. The player may immediately perform the action where the Explorer stopped. Correspondence | Yellow Envelope Move personal Stamps to an Envelope. The active player may move the Stamps from any personal stack, but may only place them onto one Envelope. If the last Stamp was removed from a stack, the player may perform the actions for the depleted stack. The players with the most and second-most Stamps placed on an Envelope will receive rewards during the Reward Phase. If there are not enough Stamps in the personal stacks, the active player may take their Stamps from the used Stamps tray. Deliver Specimen | Brown Shipping Container Place a Specimen tile in the Museum if it is researched. The player must have a Research token for the Specimen on their personal board. [Rating: 1/10] It was a nightmare, the worst experience with board games that I had for years. My good advice - remove all the sharp objects from the space around you or you can hurt yourself after 2-3hrs with this game. Better advice - don't play it.  There is soo many different things wrong with this game that it is hard to count them all, but let's try:  - it is soo dry that it can start the fire in a rain forest;  - if you are unlucky, for the first few rounds there will be no red seals available to get - what kind of game which is based on resources does not allow player to get those... it's poor design

[Rating: 1/10] A game about a racist and white supremacist:   “At some future period, not very distant as measured by centuries, the civilised races of man will almost certainly exterminate, and replace, the savage races throughout the world. At the same time the anthropomorphous apes…will no doubt be exterminated. The break between man and his nearest allies will then be wider, for it will intervene between man in a more civilized state, as we may hope, even than the Caucasian, and some ape as low as a baboon, instead of as now between the negro or Australian and the gorilla.“   -Charles Darwin, The Descent

[Rating: 1/10] I'd like to say this game is awesome. Really. But after 2 years i'm still waiting to receive it, with no news, tracking orofficial updates about shipment. Definitely my worst ks ever

[Rating: 1/10] Making 1-Star review because I'm at my wits end trying to get a reply from the developer or the publisher after my copy was stolen in delivery.  I would really like to still get a copy of the KS Deluxe Edition I ordered, but all I'm getting is radio silence.    PLEASE CONTACT ME BACK!

[Rating: 1/10] Spanish editor @Tcgfactory has provided way less product of what they promised to the shops, so a bunch of preorders have been cancelled, including mine. So no, thank you.

[Rating: 1/10] After 2 plays:  The only mechanism really matters in the plethora of options is the book multiplier track. But oh wait, if a player is the last in the round there is no chance to progress the same way as everyone else, and there is no catchup mechanism other than wasting a worker to become first after a whole round.   The game is too long and too complex for the sake of complexity, without providing real alternative ways to win or any consolation prizes for players being last in the round.

[Rating: 2/10] Missing expansions that were hidden in main objectives. Horrible rubber stamps that stick together, badly designed box and insert. Missing rules and error on some components listing. Really dissapointing.   Gameplay wise there is a huge first player advantage. Get discovery make loads money and you will continue lead for rest of game. coins mean so much in this game especially when it comes to repeating actions. And some actions are just naturally stronger especially when objective cards are drawn!

[Rating: 2/10] Heavy and plodding. All sorts of bits and bobs that don't interconnect in interesting or clever ways but look shiny on kickstarter. A pain to teach and a chore to play.
